## Shallow-water Roe and plume-roe (`type: shallow-roe`, `plume-roe`) {#sec-ch04-shallow}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0 (chengcli/snapy)
sources: OUTLINE.md 4.12
status: draft
-->

### Summary

Both of these exist for equation sets outside the main compressible path, and both are registered through the
same factory as the others. They are grouped here because neither can be selected for a compressible deck and
neither carries the face pressure the curved-grid path needs.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- Two special-purpose solvers for equation sets that are not the compressible one.
- Switches: `type: shallow-roe` for the shallow-water system, `type: plume-roe` for the plume system.
- Shallow-roe carries a height and two momenta, with no energy row and no face pressure.
- Plume-roe is not a Roe solver: it falls back to a Lax-Friedrichs flux.
:::

### Derivation

The shallow-water system has no internal energy, so the wave structure reduces to two gravity waves around a
height-weighted average. The body at {{< code src/riemann/shallow_roe_impl.h shallow_roe_impl >}} uses the same square-root
weighting as @sec-ch04-roe, with the height taking the place of the density at
`sqrtdl` ({{< code src/riemann/shallow_roe_impl.h shallow_roe_impl >}}).

That the flux covariance of @sec-ch04-fluxcov excludes the shallow-water equation of state follows directly:
the correction acts on an enthalpy flux, and this system has no row to correct.

Plume-roe is named for Roe and is not one. `forward` at {{< code src/riemann/plume_roe.cpp PlumeRoeSolverImpl::forward >}} builds the two
physical fluxes at `calculate_flux` ({{< code src/riemann/plume_roe.cpp calculate_flux >}}) and combines them with a Lax-Friedrichs average at
{{< code src/riemann/plume_roe.cpp lax_friedrichs_flux >}}: the centred flux minus half the maximum signal speed times the jump. That
is the most dissipative of the usual choices and makes no use of the characteristic structure. The name is
misleading and is recorded as such.

A port of `shallow-roe` checks that it is consistent, and that with every wave moving right it returns the left
flux, so its decomposition reproduces the jump [check `src/snapy_report/ch04/solvers_check.py`, output
`solvers_check.out`, `[C6]`]. `plume-roe` is not ported.

### Numerical method

Neither solver writes a face pressure, so neither inherits the pressure-force path of @sec-ch04-sphsrc. On a
curved grid that is not a restriction for shallow water, which is solved on the sphere through its own
geometry, but it does mean that the `prim` and face-pressure arguments of the coordinate `forward` are unused
whenever these solvers run.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `plume-roe` is a Lax-Friedrichs flux under a name that promises a characteristic solver. A reader choosing it
  for its dissipation properties will get the opposite of what the name suggests.
:::

1. **Untested.** Nothing in the repository runs the plume solver, so its behaviour is recorded from reading
   alone.
2. **No face pressure.** Neither solver can drive the curved-grid pressure force or the well-balanced path of
   @sec-ch05.
